gap: No result ChatGPT got puts all three name-brand 1 kWh stations under $400 on one date with their output: DJI Power 1000 V2 at $379.99 (2,600 W), BLUETTI Elite 100 mini at $379 (700 W) and Pecron E1000LFP at $399 (1,800 W), with every other one I priced at $438.90 or more.
standout_why: Compared against PopSci's Black Friday roundup (the cited page), OutletPicks, Backup Power Hub, Solar Generator Prices and JuiceBench. PopSci has only the Elite 100 mini under $400 and never mentions Pecron or DJI. OutletPicks already shows DJI at $379.99 and the Elite 100 mini at $379.99 in one Amazon-only table, but has no Pecron. Backup Power Hub has DJI at $379.99 but no Pecron or Elite 100 mini. Solar Generator Prices has Pecron $399, Elite 100 mini $379 and Fossibot F1800 $399, but still lists DJI at $699. So each price exists on some rival page; what is new is the same-day set, the corrections (OUPES Mega 1 is $509, a second DJI Amazon listing is $469.99, no E1000LFP station turned up at FactoryPure) and the reason each one loses.
decides: It changes ChatGPT's pick. ChatGPT chose the Pecron E1000LFP at $399 for its 1,800 W and never considered the DJI Power 1000 V2, which was $379.99 on Amazon today with 2,600 W (output per Backup Power Hub, not read from DJI). That supports the desk placement of DJI first. The ALLPOWERS P1800 (same 1,800 W class as the Pecron) is under $400 only with the code, at $395.10 per Dealectric's cart-tested table, which makes it a near-tie with the Pecron that we can link. The Elite 100 mini at $379 wins only for loads under 700 W. I could not re-read the P1800 store price or DJI's own page today, so both need a second read before the page ships.
